finding.claim: SSRF in POST /profile/avatar. The only validation is a startsWith('https://') prefix check, which does not restrict the host or IP. axios also follows redirects by default (including https to http), so the check is bypassable. An unauthenticated caller can make the server request internal or link-local hosts, such as https://169.254.169.254/, https://localhost:PORT/, https://users.internal:8080/, or an attacker server that 302-redirects to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or http://users.internal:8080/. The response body is not returned, only its byte length, so this is mostly blind SSRF. The size oracle and error behaviour still allow internal port and host probing and reaching internal endpoints with side effects.

trace.note: only checks typeof string and startsWith('https://'); no host, IP or DNS allowlist or denylist
axios.get(url) with default redirect following (maxRedirects 5) and no host restriction
response size is reflected to the caller (blind-ish oracle)

finding.guards_checked: The scheme prefix check is enforced (returns 400) but does not validate host, resolved IP or redirects. There is no auth middleware on the route, no allowlist, and no maxRedirects:0 or beforeRedirect hook. The /users/:id route at server.js:18-22 was checked and is SAFE for SSRF: the host is the fixed constant USER_SVC and the id is encodeURIComponent'd, so only the path under the fixed host can be influenced, and an id of '..' can at most normalize to /v1/. It is not reported.

verdict.guard_found: Only a typeof string and startsWith('https://') prefix check at server.js:11; no host/IP allowlist, no auth middleware, no maxRedirects limit.
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl, the only guard at server.js:11 is a scheme prefix check (not a closing guard), and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get with default redirects, with the byte length reflected at server.js:15.
